minutes.headline: Planning Board ratified Christopher Riley as land use director, sent ADU bylaw edits to the select board, and granted a one-year extension at 260 Fula Road.
minutes.summary: The Planning Board heard the Economic Development Committee on permitting roadblocks for new businesses, ratified the new land use director, and approved ADU bylaw wording for the fall special town meeting. It granted only a one-year site plan extension for 260 Fula Road (the applicant asked for two), discussed MBTA communities zoning, and approved three sets of minutes.

public_comment.topic: Roadblocks for new businesses: repetitive permit requests, parking-driven paperwork, boards waiting on each other's approvals, and the cost and delay to applicants.
Examples of unnecessary paperwork for existing spaces and sequential board approvals tripling timelines; urged town-wide streamlining.
Existing, previously approved spaces should not have to start over; also noted the parking table treats most retail under a size threshold alike.
Invited board and town officials to the town meet and greet for businesses on the Thursday the 28th.
Concern from a resident that the ADU changes remove owner-occupancy, letting investors buy and rent both units, and concern about MBTA communities pushing rental housing.

what_happened.line: The Planning Board voted to ratify Christopher Riley as land use director, as presented by the town manager; all members present were in favor.
The board voted to send the accessory dwelling unit (ADU) bylaw language to the select board for the fall special town meeting warrant.
The board granted a one-year extension of site plan approval and stormwater permit for 260 Fula Road; the minutes say the applicant asked for two years.
The Economic Development Committee described repeated permit requests and sequential board approvals that delay new businesses; staff said parking rules and process are on their radar.
On MBTA communities zoning the board only discussed it, and decided to wait for the new land use director to start before taking next steps.

why_it_matters: The ADU bylaw wording is headed for the fall special town meeting warrant, so residents may be asked to vote on it, and a resident at this meeting raised concern that it removes owner-occupancy.
Business owners' complaints about permitting cost and delay, and the pending MBTA communities zoning, point to rule changes that could reach residents' zoning and local development later.
watch_next: Planning Board meetings are set for September 23 and October 28, with none on October 14.
The select board's decision to place the ADU bylaw language on the warrant for the fall special town meeting.
